item.title: Middle East live: EU moves to widen sanctions on Iran, threats to freedom of navigation
item.description: The EU Council on Friday said in a statement that it would extend the scope of sanctions targeting Tehran's military support for Russia's war against Ukraine to include individuals and entities involved in Iran's actions to threaten the freedom of navigation in Hormuz. Follow our liveblog for the latest developments.

item.title: Regional Mediators Rush to Save U.S.-Iran Cease-Fire
item.description: Pakistan and Qatar have dispatched teams to Tehran under the looming threat of resumed war, after weeks of diplomacy failed to produce an agreement.

item.title: Alberta Will Vote on a Possible Referendum to Separate From Canada. Here’s What to Know.
item.description: Premier Danielle Smith announced that she would ask citizens to vote on whether they want to stay in Canada, or hold a referendum to secede.

item.title: Mamdani won't attend Israel Day Parade, breaking decades-long mayoral tradition amid antisemitism surge
item.description: NYC's Israel Day Parade expects record turnout after Mayor Mamdani confirmed he will not attend, drawing criticism from Jewish leaders citywide.

item.title: Israel's Ben-Gvir sees 'no innocent people in Gaza or even Europe': Journalist Gideon Levy
item.description: FRANCE 24's François Picard welcomes veteran Israeli journalist and Haaretz columnist Gideon Levy. He offers a scathing analysis of Israeli politics, the Gaza war, the unprecedented rise of xenophobic nationalism and Israel's growing dependence on the United States. Speaking from Tel Aviv amid mounting electoral tensions, Levy argues that "everything – war and peace, domestic politics, legislation – is now covered by the shadow of the upcoming elections".

item.title: 'We'll never know if he could have been saved.' The gaps in Trump's rural health fund
item.description: Republicans promise that $50 billion in new health funding will help rural America. But it's not expected to aid the years-long effort in North Carolina's Martin County to reopen its only hospital.

item.title: What to know about the death of Congolese man in Ireland
item.description: Hundreds of people in Ireland are calling for justice after the death of a Congolese man restrained by security guards in Dublin

item.title: U.S. bears brunt of Israel’s missile defense, Pentagon assessments show
item.description: Amid hostilities with Iran, the American military expended far more advanced interceptors to protect Israel than Israeli forces did, according to Defense Department data.

item.title: 'Cold, pragmatic relationship': UAE-Israel ties driven by defence and technology
item.description: Nadia Massih is pleased to welcome Dr Andreas Krieg, Senior Lecturer at the School of Security Studies at King's College London and Fellow at the Institute of Middle Eastern Studies. According to Krieg, "Iran is fighting a war against the global economy." By targeting the UAE, and especially Dubai, Tehran is not merely retaliating militarily but seeking to exploit what Krieg calls the "Achilles heel" of the international system: the Gulf's hyperconnected financial and logistical infrastructure.

item.title: Will US invade? Three ways Cuba crisis could play out now
item.description: The Trump administration has been putting tremendous economic pressure on the island's Communist government.
